reasons.realCost: Klaviyo's Email plan bill matches its published per-profile-tier sticker price, but send volume can force a costlier tier than profile count alone would suggest, as at 50,000 profiles, where the send volume needs the $860 tier rather than the $720 tier.
reasons.pricingHonesty: Every Email profile tier is shown on a public self-serve calculator alongside published starting prices for the Composer, Customer Hub, Social Marketing and Reviews add-ons, though SMS/MMS/RCS message rates and manual-billing contract terms are not disclosed on the public site.
reasons.smallTeamFit: Klaviyo is self-serve with credit-card billing and a free 250-profile tier for testing, though active accounts must monitor profile counts to avoid being auto-moved to a pricier tier at renewal.
reasons.doesTheJob: Klaviyo bundles email and SMS marketing with an AI campaign composer, an on-site customer hub, social marketing and reviews, letting an ecommerce seller consolidate several point tools into one Klaviyo account.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Self-serve Klaviyo accounts are billed and can be canceled month to month with no annual contract, though canceling mid-cycle forfeits the remainder of that month with no refund.
reasons.trackRecord: Klaviyo has operated since 2012, went public on the NYSE in 2023, and publishes a live status page covering its platform components.

basis: Klaviyo is a strong buy for an ecommerce-focused small business: its core Email pricing is transparent and scales predictably with active profiles, and its add-ons let a buyer add capability without switching platforms, though add-on sprawl and no annual discount mean the total bill can grow beyond the base plan's sticker price.
method: Two independent blind passes scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the lower of the two overall scores, because this tool runs an affiliate program we have joined or may join. Pass scores: 4 and 4.1.
